executive_summary: The dominant theme across today's report is accelerated Western and allied military capability deployment in response to sustained regional pressure, particularly in the Indo-Pacific and along NATO's eastern flank. The permanent basing of US Global Hawks in Japan represents a significant ISR posture shift signaling long-term commitment to Pacific competition, while South Korea's ahead-of-schedule frigate commissioning suggests allied navies are deliberately compressing procurement timelines. Turkey's dual naval delivery in a single ceremony is notable both operationally and diplomatically, reinforcing Ankara's role as a defense exporter to NATO partners like Romania while simultaneously expanding its own naval capacity. The absence of ICS/SCADA/OT reporting today is itself worth flagging, as it leaves a gap in the overall picture regarding potential adversary activity in critical infrastructure, which historically correlates with periods of elevated conventional military signaling.

sections.title: Military
sections.intro: Indo-Pacific force posture shifts and allied naval fleet expansions dominate today's military landscape, reflecting sustained investment in deterrence across multiple theaters.

items.headline: US permanently stations RQ-4 Global Hawks in Japan to bolster Pacific ISR coverage
items.summary: Three RQ-4 Global Hawk high-altitude reconnaissance drones are now permanently based at Yokota Air Base, marking a shift from rotational to enduring ISR presence in the Pacific. The move enhances persistent surveillance capacity over the East China Sea and Korean Peninsula without requiring temporary deployments. Watch for follow-on basing decisions that could signal further U.S. force laydown adjustments in the region.

items.headline: Turkey delivers new OPV to its own navy and a corvette to Romania in a single ceremony
items.summary: ASFAT simultaneously handed over the first Hisar-class Offshore Patrol Vessel to the Turkish Navy and a corvette to Romania, demonstrating Turkey's growing defense export capability within NATO. The dual delivery deepens Turkish-Romanian naval ties and signals Ankara's ambition to position itself as a credible regional shipbuilder. Romania's acquisition strengthens Black Sea fleet capacity at a strategically sensitive moment.

items.headline: South Korea commissions second advanced Ulsan Batch-III frigate ahead of schedule
items.summary: ROKS Gyeongbuk, the second FFX Batch-III frigate, was delivered to the ROK Navy early, continuing Seoul's accelerated naval modernization program. The Ulsan Batch-III class features improved anti-submarine warfare and air defense capabilities, directly relevant to North Korean submarine threats and broader regional competition. Early delivery suggests South Korean shipbuilders are maintaining production momentum despite global supply chain pressures.

sections.title: ICS / SCADA / OT
sections.intro: Today's ICS/SCADA/OT threat landscape is thin on high-signal reporting, with no significant vulnerability disclosures, incidents, or advisories surfacing in the past 24 hours.
